hyps.why: With edge 1->3 already removed, cutting edge 2->3 leaves only edge 0->3 into the output, which badly hurts or disconnects the network.
If edge 2->3 is already none, removing edge 0->3 leaves edge 1->3 as the only input to the output, which is much more harmful.
Putting a 3x3 conv where there was no edge restores a key computational path, so the gain is much larger than when it replaces an existing op.
Adding a residual input-to-output skip where none existed improves optimization far more than swapping out an existing op on that edge.
When edge 2->3 is none, node 2 never reaches the output, so changes to edge 0->2 have almost no effect, which erases the usual gain from a conv.
Edge 1->2 only matters through node 2, which is cut off from the output when edge 2->3 is none.
If edge 0->1 is none, node 1 carries zeros, so a conv on edge 1->3 adds nothing useful.
With node 1 dead because edge 0->1 is none, a conv on edge 1->2 processes zeros and cannot help.
Adding a conv path from node 1 to the output where there was none increases depth and capacity much more than replacing another op.
Bringing node 1 back to life by replacing none on edge 0->1 opens the downstream edges 1->2 and 1->3, giving a large gain.
